candidates.change_summary: Replace addition to balance with subtraction so msg.value is subtracted from the stored balance when depositing.
Remove the reentrancy guard effect by eliminating the require check so the modifier still toggles locked_ but doesn't prevent entry.
Return balance of msg.sender instead of the provided address, changing observed value when caller != args.
Return zero constant, making all calls return 0 regardless of stored balance.
Return balance of a fixed address (contract deployer assumed at address(0)), changing value for most inputs.
Replace the line that updates userBalance[msg.sender] with a no-op (removes the addition), so deposits do not change the stored balance.
Replace the update to set the balance to msg.value instead of adding, so balance becomes only the last deposit amount.
Remove the reentrancy protection by deleting the locking and require, allowing reentrant calls during addToBalance and withdrawBalance.
Invert the require so it requires the lock to be true, which will cause calls guarded by the modifier to revert (changing observable behavior).
Move the userBalance reset to 0 to before the external call, preventing reentrancy from draining more funds.
Omit setting userBalance to 0 after the call, leaving the balance intact so repeated withdrawals can succeed.
Remove the reentrancy lock setting so nonReentrant_ no longer prevents reentrant calls.
Set the lock only after the function body executes, allowing the guarded function to be reentered during its execution but marking locked afterwards.

Move the userBalance reset to 0 to before the external call so balance is set to 0 prior to transferring funds (prevents reentrancy affecting balance), changing post-withdraw balances for reentrant withdrawals.

Remove setting locked_ = false after the function body, so once entered the nonReentrant_ modifier never releases the lock, preventing further calls and leaving locked_ true (affects subsequent observable withdraws).
Set userBalance[msg.sender] to 1 instead of 0 after the external call, leaving a non-zero remainder in balance (observable difference).
